dialogue.content: いくらさん、おはようございます。画面に入っています。時間になりましたら、よろしくお願いいたします。
dialogue.English: Good morning, Ikura-san. I'm here in the call. We can begin when it's our scheduled time. I look forward to our session.

dialogue.content: おはようございます。よろしくお願いいたします。
dialogue.English: Good morning. Thank you for seeing me.

dialogue.content: こんにちは、相談員です。よろしくお願いします。
dialogue.English: Hello, I'm your counselor. It's nice to meet you.

dialogue.content: こんにちは、よろしくお願いします
dialogue.English: Hello, it's nice to meet you too.

dialogue.content: 今日はご相談にお越し頂きありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you for coming in for a consultation today.

dialogue.content: 初めにご年齢と性別、ご相談の中でなんとお呼びしたら良いかを教えて下さい。
dialogue.English: To start, could you please tell me your age, gender, and what you would like me to call you during our session?

dialogue.content: 35歳女性　いくらと申します
dialogue.English: I'm a 35-year-old woman. Please call me Ikura.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。いくらさん、今日はどの様なご相談でお越し頂きましたか？
dialogue.English: Thank you. Ikura-san, what brings you in today?

dialogue.content: 夫を信用できなくなってしまって、悩んでいます
dialogue.English: I'm struggling because I can no longer trust my husband.

dialogue.content: 夫さんを信用できないと思ってしまうのは辛いことですね。
dialogue.English: It must be very painful to feel that you can't trust your husband.

dialogue.content: はい…
dialogue.English: Yes...

dialogue.content: 悩まれるのも当たり前と思います。
dialogue.English: It’s completely understandable that you’re struggling with this.

dialogue.content: どの様なところが信用できないのか、教えてください。
dialogue.English: Could you tell me what it is that makes you feel you can't trust him?

dialogue.content: 去年夫が、ギャンブルで多額の借金を作っていた事が発覚しました
dialogue.English: Last year, it came to light that my husband had accumulated a large amount of debt from gambling.

dialogue.content: そして、失踪したんです
dialogue.English: And then he disappeared.

dialogue.content: それは大変なことですね。借金も、疾走も、どれほど驚かれていることでしょうと思います。
dialogue.English: That's a terrible situation. The debt, and his disappearance... I can only imagine how shocked you must have been.

dialogue.content: 失踪ごめんなさい
dialogue.English: I'm sorry, I meant his disappearance.

dialogue.content: 自殺未遂をして病院に運ばれ、連絡が来て見つかりました
dialogue.English: He was found after attempting suicide and being taken to the hospital. That's when I was contacted.

dialogue.content: そこまで行ってしまったのですね。ご連絡を受けてのご心痛、はかり知れません。大変ですね。
dialogue.English: It went that far... I can't imagine the pain you must have felt upon receiving that call. That must have been so difficult.

dialogue.content: 今現在は、どの様な状態なのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: What is his current situation?

dialogue.content: 今は、仕事にも復帰して、全然普通に見えます
dialogue.English: Right now, he's back at work and seems perfectly normal.

dialogue.content: お身体は回復なさったと言うことですね、
dialogue.English: So, his physical health has recovered, then.

dialogue.content: はい、そうですね
dialogue.English: Yes, that's right.

dialogue.content: 自殺未遂と言っても、そこまで危機的な物ではありませんでした
dialogue.English: Even though it was a suicide attempt, it wasn't a life-threatening one.

dialogue.content: そうでしたか、少し安心しました。病院から戻られてからはどの機雷の時が経っているのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: I see, that's a small relief. How long has it been since he returned from the hospital?

dialogue.content: どのくらい
dialogue.English: How long...

dialogue.content: ごめんなさい
dialogue.English: I'm sorry.

dialogue.content: もう、1年は経ってますね
dialogue.English: It's already been a year.

dialogue.content: この一年は、ご夫妻としてどの様に過ごされていらしたのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: How have you and your husband spent this past year as a couple?

dialogue.content: 金融機関ではなく、あちこちからお金を借りていたので、その整理などをしていました
dialogue.English: He had borrowed money from various places, not from financial institutions, so I've been sorting all of that out.

dialogue.content: それは大変なことですね
dialogue.English: That must be an incredible burden.

dialogue.content: そのほとんどを、私が考える感じで、夫は楽しそうに復職しています
dialogue.English: I feel like I'm the one handling almost all of it, while my husband seems to be happily back at work.

dialogue.content: ほとんどをいくらさんがなさっているのですか？
dialogue.English: So, you're handling most of it yourself, Ikura-san?

dialogue.content: それはどんなに大変なことでしょう
dialogue.English: I can't imagine how difficult that must be.

dialogue.content: そうなんです…夫は、任せっきりといった感じで
dialogue.English: Yes... My husband has completely left it up to me.

dialogue.content: 自分のことなのに、無責任だと腹が立つのは当たり前のことだと思います。
dialogue.English: It's completely understandable that you would be angry at his irresponsibility, especially since this is his own issue.

dialogue.content: 私の方が驚いているのに、夫はのんきなもんです
dialogue.English: I'm the one who's still in shock, but he's acting so carefree.

dialogue.content: 呑気な顔をみていると、また腹が立つのも当然です。返済の状況などについて、夫さんと話し合う事はあるのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Seeing him look so carefree would naturally make you angry again. Do you ever talk with your husband about the repayment situation?

dialogue.content: 最初のうちは、反省からなのか、一緒に返済計画を考えてましたね
dialogue.English: At first, perhaps out of remorse, we worked together on a repayment plan.

dialogue.content: それがいつの間にか止まってしまったのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: And did that gradually stop at some point?

dialogue.content: どんどん逃げていった感じです
dialogue.English: It feels like he gradually started avoiding it.

dialogue.content: 何か言うと、また自殺するような事を言ってきます
dialogue.English: Whenever I say something, he starts talking about attempting suicide again.

dialogue.content: まあひどい、脅かしてくるのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: That's awful. Is he threatening you?

dialogue.content: 自分はこんなに悩んでいるのに、追い詰めてきた…みたいに、被害者的な態度になります
dialogue.English: He takes on a victim-like attitude, as if to say, 'I'm already suffering so much, and you're just cornering me...'

dialogue.content: 被害者は、いくらさんであることに気づいていないのですね。
dialogue.English: He doesn't seem to realize that you are the victim here, Ikura-san.

dialogue.content: 本当に、それなんです
dialogue.English: That's exactly it.

dialogue.content: 被害者は明らかにいくらさんです。
dialogue.English: You are clearly the victim in this situation.

dialogue.content: 当初、病院から紹介された、ギャンブル依存症の会に行ってたのですが色々理由をつけて、行かなくなりました
dialogue.English: Initially, he was attending a gambling addiction support group that the hospital recommended, but he started making various excuses and stopped going.

dialogue.content: 依存症はきちんと治療しないと元に戻ると一般的には言われています。
dialogue.English: It's generally said that without proper treatment, addiction can lead to a relapse.

dialogue.content: そうですよね
dialogue.English: Yes, that's right.

dialogue.content: いくらさんもギャンブル依存症の会には同行なさったのですか？
dialogue.English: Did you also accompany him to the gambling addiction support group meetings, Ikura-san?

dialogue.content: 家族が行って良い日のには、行きました
dialogue.English: I went on the days when family members were allowed to attend.

dialogue.content: 一緒に向かい合おうとなさったのですね、とても素晴らしい行動だと思います。
dialogue.English: So you were trying to face this together. I think that's a wonderful thing to do.

dialogue.content: やめてしまった理由はわかりますか？
dialogue.English: Do you know why he stopped going?

dialogue.content: 1人で行かせるのも、心配というか、本当にちゃんと向き合う姿勢で行ってるのか不安で
dialogue.English: Letting him go alone made me worry, or rather, I was anxious about whether he was really going with the right attitude to confront the issue.

dialogue.content: 月1しかなくて、一応今も継続中にはなってますが、体調が悪いだので、全然行ってませんね
dialogue.English: It's only once a month, and while he's technically still enrolled, he hasn't been going at all, giving excuses like he doesn't feel well.

dialogue.content: でも、地域の集まりみたいな物には参加して、お酒を飲んだりしてるので、腹が立ちます
dialogue.English: But it makes me angry because he'll attend things like local community gatherings and drink alcohol.

dialogue.content: これまでのお話を少しまとめさせていただきますね
dialogue.English: Let me summarize what you've told me so far.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Okay.

dialogue.content: 夫さんがギャンブルから多額の借金をし、自殺未遂まで、
dialogue.English: Your husband accumulated a large amount of debt from gambling and even attempted suicide;

dialogue.content: その借金に一人で対応する状態
dialogue.English: you are the one dealing with the debt on your own;

dialogue.content: ギャンブル依存症の会にもあまり行かなくなっt
dialogue.English: he has mostly stopped attending the gambling addiction support group;

dialogue.content: 近所の飲み会には出かける、仕事も楽しそうにしている様に見える。
dialogue.English: he goes out to neighborhood drinking gatherings and seems to be enjoying work;

dialogue.content: 話を詰めようとすると、また自殺すると脅す。
dialogue.English: and when you try to talk to him seriously about it, he threatens to commit suicide again.

dialogue.content: 一つ質問です、それでもあなたをつなぎ止めている夫さんへの思いは何ですか？
dialogue.English: I have one question. Despite all of this, what is it about your husband that keeps you with him?

dialogue.content: やはり子供がいるので、家庭を壊したくないという事ですかね
dialogue.English: I suppose it's because we have children, and I don't want to break up the family.

dialogue.content: 夫がどうとかいうより、子供達に悟られないように、普通にしようと努力してます
dialogue.English: It's less about my husband and more about trying to act normal so the children don't notice.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね、子供さんがいらっしゃるのですね。子供さんは何人で、何歳か教えてください。
dialogue.English: I see, so you have children. Could you please tell me how many children you have and their ages?

dialogue.content: 中2，高1の2人です
dialogue.English: I have two. One is in the second year of junior high school, and the other is in the first year of high school.

dialogue.content: 多感なお年頃ですね。
dialogue.English: They are at a very sensitive age.

dialogue.content: そうなんですよね
dialogue.English: They are, aren't they?

dialogue.content: いくらさんが悟られない様にとしても、家庭内の様子は察してしまうお年頃と思いますが、どの様な様子でしょうか？
dialogue.English: Even if you try to hide it, I imagine they are at an age where they can sense the atmosphere at home. How do things seem?

dialogue.content: こんな事が発覚するまでは、夫はとても子煩悩で、家庭の事も沢山してくれる、良い夫だったんです
dialogue.English: Before all of this came to light, my husband was a doting father and a good husband who did a lot for the family.

dialogue.content: そうだったんですね
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: だから私もとても驚きましたし、しばらく失踪してた時は、子供達も驚いていましたが、自殺未遂の事や借金の事は、言ってないんです
dialogue.English: That's why I was so shocked. The children were also shocked when he was gone for a while, but I haven't told them about the suicide attempt or the debt.

dialogue.content: だから、今も、子供にとっては優しい父親でしょう
dialogue.English: So even now, to the children, he is probably still a kind father.

dialogue.content: 子供さんにとっては、お母様も大切なお母様です。
dialogue.English: To your children, you are also their precious mother.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: お母様が悩んでいる事は、子供さんは肌で感じてらっしゃると思うのです。
dialogue.English: I think your children can sense that you are struggling.

dialogue.content: 疲れてる感じには見えるでしょうね
dialogue.English: They probably notice that I look tired.

dialogue.content: 夫さんに、子供さんたちへの思いを含めて、ご自分の気持ちを伝える事が大切だと思うのですが、
dialogue.English: I think it's important to convey your feelings to your husband, including your thoughts about the children,

dialogue.content: 自殺するなどと言う脅しをいうのは、拒絶感が先に起こってしまうのだと思うのですが、いかがでしょうか、
dialogue.English: but when he threatens suicide, I imagine it creates a sense of rejection that makes it hard to talk. Is that right?

dialogue.content: どういうつもりでそう言うのか、私にはわかりませんが
dialogue.English: I don't know what his intentions are when he says that, but...

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 私が何か言う事でまた、俺なんかもういない方が良いから死ぬ、とか、消えるとか言われないかが、とても心配です
dialogue.English: I'm very worried that if I say anything, he'll say things like, 'It's better if I'm not around, so I'll die,' or 'I'll just disappear.'

dialogue.content: そうですよね、言うことが怖くなってしまいますよね
dialogue.English: Of course. It would make you afraid to say anything.

dialogue.content: 脅しで言ってるのか、そこでまた本気で、俺なんか…と思ってるのかも、ちょっとよくわからなくて…
dialogue.English: I can't quite tell if he's saying it as a threat, or if in that moment he's genuinely thinking, 'Someone like me...'

dialogue.content: ひょっとしたら、夫さんもよくわからず、言いながら、自分の気持ちに問いかけているのかもしれませんね。
dialogue.English: Perhaps your husband himself doesn’t fully understand and, as he says those things, he may be questioning his own feelings.

dialogue.content: そうなんですかね
dialogue.English: Do you think so?

dialogue.content: いくらさんの思いの伝え方で、チャレンジしてみていただきたい方法があるのですが、
dialogue.English: There is a method of communicating your feelings that I'd like you to try, Ikura-san.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Okay.

dialogue.content: あなたはこうだから、とか、あなたはこうしてよ、とかの言い方ではなく、
dialogue.English: Instead of saying things like 'You are like this,' or 'You should do this,'

dialogue.content: 私は、こう思っている。私は、こう感じてしまう。
dialogue.English: try saying, 'I think this,' or 'I feel this way.'

dialogue.content: この様に、自分の気持ちから話え行く伝え方です。
dialogue.English: It's a way of communicating that starts with your own feelings.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: あなたはこうだから！と言われると、人はまず、反発から対応してしまうのが一般的の様です。
dialogue.English: When people are told, 'You are like this!' they generally respond defensively first.

dialogue.content: でも、私はこう感じていると切り出されると、意外と思いが伝わっていくことがあります。
dialogue.English: But if you start by saying, 'I feel this way,' your thoughts can sometimes get through unexpectedly well.

dialogue.content: なるほど
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: 子供さんのことも思い、そして、家族のことを思って、責任感のあるいくらさんですから、
dialogue.English: Since you care about your children and your family, and you're such a responsible person, Ikura-san,

dialogue.content: たくさんの、愛情あるメッセージが送れると思うのです。
dialogue.English: I believe you can send many loving messages this way.

dialogue.content: 私は、夫を信用できないと思って悩んでいますが　私の考え方というよりも、夫の受け取り方が変わる？方に期待という事でしょうか
dialogue.English: I'm struggling because I can't trust my husband, but is this more about hoping his reception will change, rather than changing my own way of thinking?

dialogue.content: そうですね。まず、お話ができる様になって、そこでいよいよ生き方が違うぞと思ったら、そこで子供さんたちも交えて、家族について話し合うことも大切かと思います。
dialogue.English: That's right. First, the goal is to be able to talk to each other. Then, if at that point you feel that your ways of life are truly different, it might be important to have a discussion about the family, including the children.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: なぜ、信用出来ないのか、と言う原因もはっきりしてくるかもしれません。
dialogue.English: The reason why you can't trust him might also become clearer.

dialogue.content: そこはとてもわかっていて
dialogue.English: I’m very clear on that part,

dialogue.content: 夫の外面の良さと、裏でしてきた事の二面性ですね…
dialogue.English: it’s the duality between his good outward appearance and what he has been doing behind the scenes...

dialogue.content: 信用出来ない理由は、はっきりとわかっていらっしゃるのですね。
dialogue.English: So you have a clear understanding of the reasons why you can't trust him.

dialogue.content: 今日までの理由は、そう感じていました
dialogue.English: Up until today, that's how I've felt about the reasons.

dialogue.content: ここから変わるかどうかは、今はまだよくわからないですが…
dialogue.English: Whether things will change from here on out, I still don’t really know…

dialogue.content: 変われるなら、楽だなーって
dialogue.English: If things could change, it would be such a relief.

dialogue.content: でも、話す事、試してみます
dialogue.English: But I'll try talking to him.

dialogue.content: はい、ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Yes, thank you.

dialogue.content: 会話が変わることで、気持ちの交流が変わるかもしれません。
dialogue.English: By changing the conversation, the way you connect emotionally might also change.

dialogue.content: そうですね、何かをやってみない事には…ですね
dialogue.English: That's true. Nothing will change if I don't try something.

dialogue.content: あなたは！メッセージを少しおやすみして、私は…、メッセージを試してみてください。
dialogue.English: Please take a little break from the 'You...' messages and try using 'I...' messages.

dialogue.content: わかりました
dialogue.English: I will.

dialogue.content: そんな中で、あなたのお気持ちがだんだん伝わり、夫さんがなぜそうなのかも、見えてくるかもしれません。
dialogue.English: In that process, your feelings may gradually get through to him, and you might also begin to see why your husband is the way he is.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 大きな借金に、一人で立ち向かおうとしているあなたですから、こんなご提案も受け入れてくださるかと思いました。
dialogue.English: Since you are someone who is trying to face this large debt on your own, I thought you might be receptive to this suggestion.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: 少しでもおらくになられる様にの思います。今日はご相談に来てくださってありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: I hope you can feel even a little bit of relief. Thank you for coming in for a consultation today.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございました
dialogue.English: Thank you very much.

dialogue.content: またご相談してみたいと思われた時には、気軽に来ていただけたら嬉しいです。
dialogue.English: If you ever feel you'd like to talk again, please don't hesitate to come back.

dialogue.content: はい、ありがとうございます
dialogue.English: Yes, thank you.

dialogue.content: 終了させていただきますが、よろしいでしょうか？
dialogue.English: May I bring the session to a close now?

dialogue.content: はい、大丈夫です
dialogue.English: Yes, that's fine.

dialogue.content: 今日はありがとうございました。それではカウンセリングを終了致します。
dialogue.English: Thank you for your time today. This concludes our counseling session.
